maria-ng: Ran a batch of allocator-knob experiments this morning on p4d-prod (seq=4096 workloads). Using expandable_segments=true + max_split_size_mb=64. Started hitting intermittent OOMs after ~2k tokens for some traces.

akash-k: Can you paste the memory_summary and the exact knob values you used?

maria-ng: Sure — config used:
```
{
  "expandable_segments": true,
  "max_split_size_mb": 64,
  "garbage_collection_threshold": 0.6,
  "workspace_mb": 1024
}
```
And a trimmed memory dump from the repro run (after the OOM):
```
Reserved: 23.4 GB
Allocated: 19.8 GB
Active allocations: 1342
Free segments: 118
Fragmentation estimate: 15.5%
Largest free chunk: 80 MB
Peak alloc pattern: attention kernel switch spike at seq ~2048 -> +420 MB transient
```

jane-l: Interesting — the attention kernel swap at 2048 lines up with kernel-selection heuristics we recently landed. When the kernel switches, it briefly allocates larger temp buffers for optimized matmuls, then frees them, but with expandable_segments=true the allocator tries to split/expand segments which increases internal bookkeeping churn. That can push fragmentation up during sustained KV cache growth.

sasha: TL;DR: split churn + kernel-switch transient allocations -> fragmentation + delayed GC -> OOM. Two quick ideas: 1) lower garbage_collection_threshold to 0.4 so we trigger reclamation earlier, 2) make max_split_size_mb adaptive by seq length (bigger splits for long sequences).

maria-ng: I tried lowering GC to 0.45 in a follow-up run — fewer OOMs but throughput dropped ~3% due to more frequent GC pauses. Numbers: successful runs 7/8 vs 3/8 baseline, avg token latency +3%.

perf-bot: Profiling link: https://perf.redwood/job/alloc-sweep/1961122334 (profile contains nvprof + allocator traces).

akash-k: Can we get allocator flame (timeline) around the kernel-switch event? Need to see whether splits or merges dominate. If splits dominate, increasing max_split_size_mb to 128 might reduce number of small splits. But that may increase worst-case fragmentation if large free slots are wasted.

tony-g: Small data point: on a different workload we set expandable_segments=false and max_split_size_mb=32. That reduced bookkeeping and eliminated the transient peak but we saw slightly higher steady-state reserved mem (because we don't coalesce upward). No OOMs though.

jane-l: Suggestion: run a 2x2 sweep: expandable_segments {true,false} x max_split_size_mb {32,128} with garbage_collection_threshold {0.45,0.6}. Measure: peak reserved, fragmentation %, number of GC events, token throughput. Also capture kernel-selection boundaries (seq where kernel changes).

sasha: Proposed quick patch (proof-of-concept) to avoid large temp allocations overlapping with split operations — add an "eager_gc_on_kernel_switch" flag that triggers a non-blocking reclamation step right before/after a kernel swap:
```
// allocator pseudo
if (kernel_is_switching && config.eager_gc_on_kernel_switch) {
  allocator.schedule_background_gc();
}
```

maria-ng: I implemented a prototype of eager GC and ran a 4-hour run: OOMs went to 0, throughput neutral (+0.2%). Fragmentation averaged ~12% vs 15% baseline. Patch is at: gitlab.com/redwood/alloc/merge_requests/254.

akash-k: Nice. Can you also add a metric: allocator.gc_pause_ms and allocator.split_ops_rate to the tracing so Console can alert when split_ops_rate spikes? We can auto-roll the workspace_mb down/up based on split_ops_rate + fragmentation.

maria-ng: Will add that. Quick sample trace snippet to show split storm:
```
[12:03:21] split_ops: 420/s, merge_ops: 4/s, gc_events: 1, frag_est: 22%
[12:03:22] split_ops: 512/s, attention_kernel: optimized_v2, transient_peak: +480MB
```

jane-l: Action items:
- maria-ng: run the 2x2 sweep and upload perf summaries (ETA EOD Tue)
- sasha: turn PoC eager_gc_on_kernel_switch into a feature flag and add non-blocking reclaim (ETA Thu)
- akash-k: wire metrics for split_ops_rate and allocator.gc_pause_ms into Console alerts (ETA Fri)
- tony-g: run a long-living KV-cache heavy sim with expandable_segments=false to compare fragmentation over 24h (ETA Wed)

maria-ng: Sounds good. I'll include the kernel-selection boundaries in the sweep so we can correlate exact seq thresholds. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
